messages.author: 486a8894d0e8cc54
messages.subject: rhbase, thrift serialization
parts:
Antonio, 

rhadoop is a great framework and thanks for getting it on github. 

I have been using R for a while developing some machine learning algorithms. I have rhadoop setup, and am using hbase-thrift (bin/hbase thrift start) to get to hbase. What I see is that information is getting serialized in rhbase (R's default serialize function), but, it seems that it is not getting deserialized going through hbase-thrift. 

When I scan a table while in the hbase shell, there is extra Hex code prepended to a key for a a row I inserted from R/rhbase using hb.insert, compared to if I inserted a row directly in hbase using ruby. 

key should be: 1054412861, 

but instead it is: X\x0A\x00\x00\x00\x02\x00\x02\x0D\x01\x00\x02\x03\x00\x00\x00\x00\x10\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x09\x00\x00\x00\x0A1054412861 

Do you recognize this problem that I am having? 

I wonder if I have to: 1) enable thrift to deserialize 2) start up thrift a different way 3) disable serialization in rhbase, or use a different serializer. 

I started to dive into the R code supporting rhbase, it is starting to make sense to me. Maybe I can help out sometime in the future ;-). 

Thanks, 

Owen

messages.author: 63023c771a070260
messages.subject: Re: rhbase, thrift serialization
parts:
What is happening, I believe, is that rhbase uses the default R serialization. There is no implementation outside R of that serialization and hbase sees just the raw bytes. We would need a thrift implementation in R to be able to do what you want, I think that's your proposal number 3. Also take a look at typedbytes (HADOOP-1722) and see if that can help (we have an R serde implementation for that). Once you have that the major rhbase calls are parametrized w.r.t. serde.

Antonio

Hi Owen,

I had exactly the same problem. As Antonio says, this Hex code is
added by R during serialization. HBase is not able to unserialize R
objects on the other hand.

The solution I used is 3): as a test, add parameters sz=charToRaw,
usz=rawToChar and try to write strings only. ^^

I wrote more code to be able to encode more types and read them from
Java, but except for the Java long issue, Antonio did it better within
his typed.bytes implementation. The problem raised after is that you
need to know the types of the objects you put into HBase.

--
Xavier

messages.author: 078da313710daa3c
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#2] rhbase, thrift serialization
parts:
> I have been using R for a while developing some machine learning
> algorithms. I have rhadoop setup, and am using hbase-thrift (bin/hbase
> thrift start) to get to hbase. What I see is that information is getting
> serialized in rhbase (R's default serialize function), but, it seems
> that it is not getting deserialized going through hbase-thrift.

hbase-thrift does not do serialization. "hbase shell" does only "string"
unserialization when you read (from the shell) and... that's all. Even
if you write from Java, the float which is encoded cannot be read
through hbase shell.

--
Xavier

parts:
Xaxier,

Thanks for the feedback!. 

I literally came to the same solution this morning in the use of rawToChar and charToRaw. 
And I agree there may be a need to store more than strings in the future. 

I did this after reviewing the current hbase.r file from git and its use of R's serialize and unserialize functions (as defaulted in hb.init).
---------------
hb.scan <- function(tablename,startrow, end=NULL,colspec,sz=hb.defaults("sz"), usz=hb.defaults("usz"),
                    hbc=hb.defaults("hbc")){
  ## Scans thr
  if(missing(colspec)) stop("Enter a colspec vector, e.g. c('x:f','x:u')")
  if(!is.null(end)){
    ## type <- c("prefix","stop")[pmatch(type,c("prefix","stop"))]
    ## if(is.na(type)) stop("type is either prefix or stop")
    ## if(is.null(end) && type=="stop") stop("Must provide a filter when type is stop")
    ## scanner <- if(type=="stop"){
    scanner <- .Call("hbScannerOpenFilter",hbc,tablename, sz(startrow),sz(end),colspec,as.integer(0))
    ## }else {
    ## .Call("hbScannerOpenFilter",hbc,tablename, sz(startrow),sz(filter),colspec,as.integer(1))
    ## }
  }else{
    scanner <- .Call("hbScannerOpenFilter",hbc,tablename, sz(startrow),sz(filter),colspec,as.integer(2))
  }
  mu <- function(batchsize=1000){
    x <- .Call("hbScannerGetList",hbc,scanner, as.integer(batchsize))
    lapply(x,function(r) list(usz(r[[1]]),r[[2]],lapply(r[[3]],usz)))
  }
  fu <- function(){
    invisible(.Call("hbCloseScanner",hbc,scanner))
  }
  return(list(get=mu,close=fu))
}
------------------

> hbase-thrift does not do serialization
Currently, I am just trying to understand what can be done between the systems to better handle serialization issues. The type of serialization done within rhbase is per data type. 

> hbase The problem raised after is that you need to know the types of the objects you put into HBase.
I haven't dug in to deep into hbase-thrift, or the library supporting hbase.r (hbScannerOpenFilter, hbScannerGetList, ...), but I know that thrift has a simple JSON protocol to exchange data.

org.apache.thrift.protocol.TSimpleJSONProtocol.

I am not yet familiar with the messaging between rhbase and hbase-thrift yet to make any recommendations. 

After I get data from our hbase cluster I will do some preliminary investigations on machine learning to contrast it to my previous work with R and PostgreSQL. 

Thanks!
Owen

After I got R rhbase talking to hbase via thrift, by replacing sz and usz with rawToChar and charToRaw. 

assign("sz", charToRaw,env=rhbase:::.hbEnv)

assign("usz",rawToChar,,env=rhbase:::.hbEnv)


I started to get the following error… 

Error in sz(filter) : argument must be a character vector of length 1

I noticed that the variable 'filter' is never initialized so I rewrote hb.scan as follows (just adding in a default initializer for filter in the function call), and added the function in the R command window to test it out.

    ## scanner <- if(type=="stop"){
    scanner <- .Call("hbScannerOpenFilter",hbc,tablename, sz(startrow),sz(end),colspec,as.integer(0))
    ## }else {
    ## .Call("hbScannerOpenFilter",hbc,tablename, sz(startrow),sz(filter),colspec,as.integer(1))
    ## }
  }else{
    scanner <- .Call("hbScannerOpenFilter",hbc,tablename, sz(startrow),sz(filter),colspec,as.integer(2))
  }
  mu <- function(batchsize=1000){
    x <- .Call("hbScannerGetList",hbc,scanner, as.integer(batchsize))
    lapply(x,function(r) list(usz(r[[1]]),r[[2]],lapply(r[[3]],usz)))
  }
  fu <- function(){

hb.init <- function(host='127.0.0.1', port=9090, buffsize=3*1024*1024, serialize=c("native", "raw"))
